rationale:
Decision: split into 4 children. All four are comparator-accepted declarations reused with byte-identical frozen types, so no new DAG node is created.

Why split, and why these children. The supplied proof is Simon Ch. 6, 3.3–3.9 (Lemma 3.9) for f = L, made complete by the bi-Lipschitz/area-formula facts A1–A8. The selected node cannot use any accepted DAG result unless it is a child, and one Lean proof of A1–A8 and B0–B10 would run to thousands of lines. The whole content of B2–B10 — L_#τ(M, θ, ξ) is integer multiplicity, with R.action(L^#ω) as its action — is the comparator-accepted Submission.dtc_bc_lc_pushforward (child pushforward). That declaration is Simon 2.23–2.24 and 3.3–3.9 for maps C¹ near a compact support; f := L is a special case. Its accepted Lean proof implements clause (ii) through the accepted subtree of dtc_bc_lc_pf_pushforward_isIntegerMultiplicity, which is the supplied construction step for step:
- refined bi-Lipschitz pieces = A5, A6, B2, B5;
- piece orientation = B3, B4;
- the one-piece push-forward with dpf_approxTangent_ae_bilipschitz_piece = B5–B9 per piece and A7, the supplied repair of Simon's unproved (3.7);
- gluing with an integer density = B6–B8, B10.
A fresh-named copy would duplicate about 75 accepted nodes. The push-forward theorem is stated for currents, not triples. Three more accepted declarations translate between the two, and they also give the carrier bound the frozen type demands:
- imrep_current (dtc_imrep_current, Simon 6.3.1): R defines the current T.
- mass_support (dor_imrep_massOn_eq_measure_and_support, Simon 6.2.12, 6.3.2(3)): spt T = spt μ_R, and likewise for any representation of L_#T.
- trim_carrier (dtc_imrep_of_null_off_compact): restricts a representation to a compact set off which its carrier is null.
Precedent: the selected node's parent, dimred_cs_minimizing_of_minimizing_in_subspace, has a byte-identical twin, idtp_fons_cs_minimizing_of_minimizing_in_subspace. The twin was accepted on 2026-10-14 (candidate bbd0cdeeba21a078ed0172b4be518ef55f43e257). Its decomposition-v2 reuses dtc_bc_lc_pushforward the same way, for the linear projection q.

Departure from the supplied proof, stated explicitly. The supplied proof reads the carrier bound N ⊆ L(K) off its construction (N ⊆ N₀ ⊆ L(K), B5, B10). Here it comes from the support clause spt L_#T ⊆ L(spt T) ⊆ L(K) of the push-forward theorem (Simon 2.23–2.24), combined with spt = spt μ for representations and a null-set trimming of the carrier. That trimming is the supplied B1 argument (θ ≥ 1) together with A2. Everything else is the supplied argument, used through the reused declaration.

Mapping (supplied step → where it is proved):

Parent assembly. This is the selected node's Lean proof from the four frozen children, Lean-checked. Notation: M := R.carrier, θ := R.mult, ξ := R.orient, μ_R := R.measure, Hᵐ := μHE[m], L^#ω := affinePullbackForm L 0 ω.
P1. Since m ≥ 1, write m = k + 1.
P2 (Simon 6.3.1). imrep_current with U := ℝ^P gives T ∈ 𝒟_m(ℝ^P) with T(ω) = R.action(ω) for every test form ω (R.Represents T).
P3 (supplied B1, via the support). mass_support with U := ℝ^P (open) gives spt T = spt μ_R.
- Kᶜ is an open set with μ_R(Kᶜ) = 0, so it misses spt μ_R. Hence spt T ⊆ K.
- spt μ_R is closed, so spt T is compact.
P4 (Simon 2.23–2.24, 3.3–3.9 = supplied B2–B10). Apply pushforward with dimension k + 1, O := ℝ^P and f := L. L is C¹ with fderiv ℝ L x = L. With Y := T and its representation R it gives push:
- (i) push T(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)ξ(x)((ω(Lx)).compContinuousLinearMap L) dHᵐ = R.action(L^#ω), since L^#ω(x) = (ω(0 + Lx)).compContinuousLinearMap L;
- (ii) push T is integer multiplicity, so some R'' : IMRep univ m represents it;
- (iii) spt push T ⊆ L(spt T) ⊆ L(K).
P5. L(K) is compact (a continuous image), hence closed and Borel.
- mass_support for push T and R'' gives spt μ_{R''} = spt push T ⊆ L(K).
- The complement of the support is μ_{R''}-null (Measure.measure_compl_support), so μ_{R''}(L(K)ᶜ) = ∫_{M''∖L(K)} θ'' dHᵐ = 0.
- Since θ'' ≥ 1 on M'' (mult_pos), Hᵐ(M'' ∖ L(K)) = 0.
P6. trim_carrier with U = V := ℝ^P and the compact set L(K) gives R' : IMRep univ m with R'.carrier ⊆ L(K) and R'.action(ω) = R''.action(ω) for every m-form ω.
P7. For ω ∈ 𝒟ᵐ(ℝ^P): R'.action(ω) = R''.action(ω) = push T(ω) = R.action(L^#ω), by P6, R''.Represents (push T) and P4(i). Together with R'.carrier ⊆ L '' K this is the frozen statement.

subproblems.title: An integer multiplicity triple defines a current
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, and R = (M, θ, ξ) an IMRep of U (Simon 6.3.1 data). Then there is T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) such that T(ω) = R.action ω = ∫_M θ(x)⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ dHⁿ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (R.Represents T). Here T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) means a GeometricCurrentOn U n: a linear functional on 𝒟ⁿ(U) with T(ω_j) → 0 whenever ω_j → 0 in Simon's test-form topology (TestFormOnConverges).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n), ∃ T : GeometricCurrentOn U n, R.Represents T
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse note (context, not part of the numbered proof): this child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.dtc_imrep_current of DAG node root.density_and_tangent_cones-a1.localize-a1.imrep_current-a1 (status accepted, candidate commit 642d7450f79f28435ddba02f9c815e2208bcee00; its comparator-v1.log ends with "Your solution is okay!" and its accepted-candidate audit records comparator_passed = true). Its frozen type is byte-identical to the lean_statement above, so the controller reuses that node and creates no new node. Its dependency closure is accepted and contains neither the selected node nor any of its ancestors. The phrase 'the parent proof uses this in step 6.6' in the accepted proof refers to that node's own parent; the proof below cites no other declaration. Correspondence with the selected node's supplied proof: Simon 6.3.1 (chapter-06.txt lines 733–753): the triple R = (M, θ, ξ) of the supplied proof defines the current T = τ(M, θ, ξ). The supplied proof works with R.action directly; the reused push-forward theorem is stated for currents, so T is formed first. Use in the selected node: assembly step P2, with U := ℝ^P: it gives T ∈ 𝒟_m(ℝ^P) with T(ω) = R.action(ω) for every test form ω (R.Represents T).

Accepted proof:
Source: Simon 6.3.1 (chapter-06.txt lines 733–753), where formula (‡) is asserted to define a current. The parent proof uses this in step 6.6 for X̃ = τ(M_X ∩ K, θ_X, ξ_X) in U.
Notation: μ := Hⁿ⌞M = μHE[n].restrict M; for a covector α, ‖α‖ is its operator norm as a continuous alternating map.
1. Unit orientations have norm at most one. By the field orients, for μ-a.e. x there are a subspace Q and an orthonormal family τ = (τ₁, …, τₙ) such that ξ(x)(α) = α(τ) for all α, or ξ(x)(α) = −α(τ) for all α (IsUnitOrientationOf). Then for every covector α, |ξ(x)(α)| = |α(τ₁, …, τₙ)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏ᵢ|τᵢ| = ‖α‖ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm; the product is empty when n = 0).
2. Measurability. For every continuous n-form ω, the function x ↦ θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(x)) is μ-a.e. strongly measurable. Indeed θ is measurable (ℕ-valued), ξ is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (field aestronglyMeasurable_orient), ω is continuous, and evaluation (L, α) ↦ L(α) is continuous because it is bounded bilinear (isBoundedBilinearMap_apply; Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable₂).
3. θ is integrable over compact sets. Let K be compact with K ⊆ U. Then 1_K θ is μ-integrable: it is measurable, and ∫ 1_K θ dμ = ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ by the field locallyIntegrable_mult, since (Hⁿ⌞M)⌞K = Hⁿ⌞(K ∩ M) (Measure.restrict_restrict; integrable_indicator_iff). Write C_K := ∫ 1_K θ dμ ∈ [0, ∞).
4. Integrability of the integrand. Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), K := tsupport ω (compact, ⊆ U), and B := sup_y ‖ω(y)‖ < ∞ (ω is continuous with compact support). By step 1, for μ-a.e. x, |θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(x))| ≤ θ(x)‖ω(x)‖ ≤ B·1_K(x)θ(x); if x ∉ K then ω(x) = 0. By steps 2–3 and domination (Integrable.mono'), x ↦ θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(x)) is μ-integrable.
5. Linearity. Define T(ω) := R.action ω for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). Each ξ(x) is linear, so the integrand for ω + η is the sum of the integrands for ω and η. Both are integrable by step 4, so T(ω + η) = T(ω) + T(η) (integral_add). The integrand for cω is c times the integrand for ω, so T(cω) = cT(ω) (integral_const_mul). Thus T is a linear functional on 𝒟ⁿ(U), and R.Represents T holds by definition.
6. Sequential continuity. Let ω_j → 0 in 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0). Then there is a compact K ⊆ U with tsupport ω_j ⊆ K for all j, and every derivative converges uniformly on K. For the 0-th derivative (‖D⁰g(x)‖ = ‖g(x)‖ and D⁰0 = 0) this says ε_j := sup_{x∈K} ‖ω_j(x)‖ → 0. By step 1, for μ-a.e. x, |θ(x)ξ(x)(ω_j(x))| ≤ ε_j·1_K(x)θ(x), since ω_j(x) = 0 off K. Hence |T(ω_j)| ≤ ε_j·C_K (norm_integral_le_of_norm_le with step 3). Given ε > 0, choose N such that ‖ω_j(x)‖ < ε/(C_K + 1) for all j ≥ N and x ∈ K. Then |T(ω_j)| ≤ εC_K/(C_K + 1) < ε for j ≥ N, so T(ω_j) → 0.
7. By steps 5 and 6, T is a GeometricCurrentOn U n with T(ω) = R.action ω for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). ∎
proof_key_steps: Unit orientations satisfy |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ ‖α‖ for a.e. x in M.
For a test form ω the integrand is a.e. strongly measurable and dominated by sup|ω|·1_{spt ω}·θ, which is integrable by local integrability of θ. Hence ω ↦ ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ is linear.
If ω_j → 0 in 𝒟ⁿ(U) with supports in a compact K, then |T(ω_j)| ≤ sup_K|ω_j|·∫_{M∩K} θ → 0, so T is a current.

subproblems.title: Mass formula and support of an integer multiplicity current (Simon 6.3.2(3), 6.2.12)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n be natural numbers, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), and R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity triple in U (IMRep: M ⊆ U Borel and countably n-rectifiable, θ : ℝ^P → ℕ measurable with θ ≥ 1 on M and ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, ξ Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable and, Hⁿ-a.e. on M, equal to ±τ₁∧⋯∧τₙ for an orthonormal basis τ of the approximate tangent space) with T = τ(M, θ, ξ), i.e. T(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ for all ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). Let μ_R = θHⁿ⌞M (R.measure). Then (i) M_W(T) = μ_R(W) in [0, ∞] for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P, where M_W(T) is the supremum of T(ω) over ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with spt ω ⊆ W and Euclidean coefficient norm |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x; (ii) spt T = U ∩ spt μ_R.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → R.Represents T → (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → T.massOn W = R.measure W) ∧ T.support = U ∩ R.measure.support

Its frozen type is byte-identical to the lean_statement above, so the controller reuses that node and creates no new node. Its dependency closure is accepted and contains neither the selected node nor any of its ancestors. The accepted proof below is self-contained (the node was itself split into the accepted dor_ims_* children). Correspondence with the selected node's supplied proof: it supplies spt T = U ∩ spt μ_R (Simon 6.2.11–2.12, 6.3.2(3)). This is used twice in place of the localization argument of the supplied step B1. First, μ_R(Kᶜ) = 0 gives spt T ⊆ K, so T has compact support. Second, for a representation R'' of L_#T, spt μ_{R''} = spt L_#T ⊆ L(K), so μ_{R''}(L(K)ᶜ) = 0. With θ'' ≥ 1 (the B1 argument) the carrier of R'' is then Hᵐ-a.e. inside L(K). Use in the selected node: assembly steps P3 and P5, both with U := ℝ^P (open); only part (ii), the support identity, is used.

Accepted proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, Remark 3.2(3) (chapter-06.txt lines 763–765: M_W(T) = ∫_{M∩W} θ dHⁿ for open W) and Ch. 6, 2.11–2.12 (chapter-06.txt lines 295–307: spt T = spt μ_T). The book states both without proof; a complete proof follows. Notation: M = R.carrier, θ = R.mult, ξ = R.orient, μ_R = R.measure = θHⁿ⌞M. For an n-covector α, |α| = (Σ_I α(e_I)²)^{1/2} is the Euclidean coefficient norm (covectorEuclideanNorm; I runs over strictly increasing multi-indices, e_I = (e_{i_1}, …, e_{i_n})), and dx^I denotes the coordinate covector with dx^I(e_J) = δ_{IJ}. ⟨α, ξ(x)⟩ means ξ(x)(α).
1. Pointwise algebra. Let x ∈ M be a point where R.orients holds: there are an orthonormal family τ₁, …, τₙ and s ∈ {1, −1} with ⟨α, ξ(x)⟩ = s·α(τ₁, …, τₙ) for every α. Expanding τ_j = Σ_i τ_j^i e_i, multilinearity and alternation give α(τ₁, …, τₙ) = Σ_I α(e_I)·det(τ^I), where det(τ^I) is the n×n minor of the matrix (τ_j^i) on the rows I; by the Cauchy–Binet formula Σ_I det(τ^I)² = det(τᵀτ) = 1. By Cauchy–Schwarz, |⟨α, ξ(x)⟩| ≤ |α| for every α. The covector ξ^♭(x) := Σ_I ⟨dx^I, ξ(x)⟩ dx^I has coefficients s·det(τ^I), hence |ξ^♭(x)| = 1 and ⟨ξ^♭(x), ξ(x)⟩ = Σ_I det(τ^I)² = 1. (For n = 0 the only I is empty: |α| = |α()|, ξ(x) = ±evaluation, ξ^♭(x) = ±1.) Since R.orients holds Hⁿ-a.e. on M and μ_R ≪ Hⁿ⌞M, these facts hold μ_R-a.e. The field x ↦ ξ^♭(x) is μ_R-a.e. strongly measurable, being a continuous linear function of the a.e. strongly measurable ξ (R.aestronglyMeasurable_orient).
2. Integral formula. For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) the function x ↦ θ(x)⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ is Hⁿ⌞M-integrable: it is a.e. strongly measurable, vanishes off the compact set spt ω ⊆ U, is bounded by θ·sup|ω| a.e. (step 1), and ∫_{M∩spt ω} θ dHⁿ < ∞ (R.locallyIntegrable_mult). Hence T(ω) = R.action(ω) = ∫ ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ_R (integral with respect to the density θ).
3. Upper bound. Let W be open and ω admissible for M_W(T) (ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), spt ω ⊆ W, |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x). By step 1, ⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ ≤ |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for μ_R-a.e. x, and ω = 0 off W, so T(ω) ≤ μ_R(W) by step 2. Taking the supremum, M_W(T) ≤ μ_R(W).
4. Lower bound. Let W be open and t a real number with t < μ_R(W); we construct an admissible ω with T(ω) > t, which proves M_W(T) ≥ μ_R(W) (also when μ_R(W) = ∞). Put G := W ∩ U (open). Since M ⊆ U, μ_R(G) = μ_R(W). μ_R is a Borel measure, finite on compact subsets of U; restricted to the open σ-compact set G it is a Radon measure (Simon Ch. 1, 1.15), hence inner regular by compact sets and outer regular on sets of finite measure. Fix η > 0 and a compact K ⊆ G with μ_R(K) > t + 4η. (a) Lusin (Simon Ch. 1, 1.17): there is a compact K' ⊆ K with μ_R(K ∖ K') < η such that ξ^♭ restricted to K' is continuous, and |ξ^♭| = 1, ⟨ξ^♭, ξ⟩ = 1 μ_R-a.e. on K'. (b) There is an open V with K' ⊆ V, V̄ compact, V̄ ⊆ G, and μ_R(V ∖ K') < η. (c) Extend the coefficients of ξ^♭ on K' continuously to ℝ^P (Tietze), compose with the radial retraction of Λⁿ(ℝ^P) onto its closed unit ball for |·|, and multiply by a continuous χ with 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1, χ = 1 on K', spt χ ⊆ V. The resulting continuous g has compact support in V, |g| ≤ 1 everywhere and g = ξ^♭ on K'. (d) Let g_ε := φ_ε ∗ g (coefficientwise convolution with a standard mollifier). For 0 < ε < dist(spt g, ℝ^P ∖ V), g_ε is C^∞ with compact support in V ⊆ W ∩ U, |g_ε(x)| ≤ ∫ φ_ε(x − y)|g(y)| dy ≤ 1 by convexity of the norm, and g_ε → g uniformly as ε → 0; so g_ε is admissible for M_W(T). (e) By steps 2 and 1, T(g_ε) = ∫⟨g_ε, ξ⟩ dμ_R ≥ ∫_{K'}⟨g, ξ⟩ dμ_R − ∫_{V∖K'}|⟨g, ξ⟩| dμ_R − sup|g_ε − g|·μ_R(V̄) ≥ μ_R(K') − η − sup|g_ε − g|·μ_R(V̄) ≥ μ_R(K) − 2η − sup|g_ε − g|·μ_R(V̄) > t + 2η − sup|g_ε − g|·μ_R(V̄). As μ_R(V̄) < ∞, T(g_ε) > t for small ε. Together with step 3 this proves (i): M_W(T) = μ_R(W).
5. Support. By definition (SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn.support; Simon 2.11) spt T = U ∖ Z, where Z is the union of all open W with W̄ compact, W̄ ⊆ U and T(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with spt ω ⊆ W. Recall x ∈ spt μ_R iff μ_R(B) > 0 for every neighbourhood B of x. (a) If x ∈ U ∩ spt μ_R and x ∈ Z, choose W in the union with x ∈ W; every admissible form for M_W(T) has T(ω) = 0, so M_W(T) = 0, hence μ_R(W) = 0 by (i), contradicting x ∈ spt μ_R. So U ∩ spt μ_R ⊆ spt T. (b) spt T ⊆ U by definition. If x ∈ U ∖ spt μ_R, choose r > 0 with μ_R(B_r(x)) = 0 and B̄_r(x) ⊆ U (U open). For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with spt ω ⊆ B_r(x), T(ω) = ∫⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ_R = 0 by step 2; so B_r(x) is one of the sets forming Z, x ∈ Z and x ∉ spt T. Hence spt T = U ∩ spt μ_R, which is (ii).
proof_key_steps: For a unit simple n-vector ξ, |⟨α, ξ⟩| ≤ |α| (Cauchy–Binet), with equality for the dual covector ξ^♭.
T(ω) = ∫⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ_R, so admissible forms give T(ω) ≤ μ_R(W).
Lusin, Tietze extension, retraction and mollification of ξ^♭ give admissible forms with T(ω) arbitrarily close to μ_R(W).
The mass formula identifies the zero region of T with the complement of spt μ_R in U.

subproblems.title: Push-forward of compactly supported integer multiplicity currents by a map that is C¹ near the support (Simon 6.2.23–2.29, 3.3–3.9)
subproblems.statement:
Let P, m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, O ⊆ ℝ^P open, and f : ℝ^P → ℝ^P C¹ on O (ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f O). Then there is a map push : 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) → 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with the following properties.
(A) Let Y ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) be integer multiplicity with spt Y compact and spt Y ⊆ O, and let (M, θ, ξ) be any integer multiplicity representation of Y. Then:
 (i) push Y(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)·⟨ω(f(x)) ∘ ΛⁿDf(x), ξ(x)⟩ dHⁿ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P). Here (ω(f(x)) ∘ ΛⁿDf(x))(v₁, …, vₙ) = ω(f(x))(Df(x)v₁, …, Df(x)vₙ); in Lean, (ω (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x).
 (ii) push Y is integer multiplicity.
 (iii) spt push Y ⊆ f(spt Y).
 (iv) For every real L with ‖Df(y)‖ ≤ L for all y ∈ O, M(push Y) ≤ Lⁿ·M(Y), as ENNReal.ofReal (L^n) * M(Y).
 (v) If ∂Y = 0, then ∂(push Y) = 0.
(B) push(Y₁ − Y₂) = push Y₁ − push Y₂ for all integer multiplicity Y₁, Y₂ ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with compact supports contained in O.
This is f_#Y of Simon 2.24(2) and 3.9.

Accepted proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, chapter-06.txt lines 404–530 and 770–860, with the area formula of Ch. 3, 2.4–2.6:
 • 2.23–2.24: push-forward and its boundary, and the explicit formula 2.24(2) for currents with locally finite mass and C¹ maps;
 • 2.27–2.29: homotopy estimate and mollified maps;
 • 3.3–3.9: push-forward of integer multiplicity currents by locally Lipschitz maps that are proper on the support; by 3.9, f_#T is integer multiplicity.
This is the result cited as (C3) in step 6 of the parent proof, with the properties listed there. The printed arguments are copied and specialised to a map f that is C¹ on an open set O containing the compact support. Two facts the source uses tacitly are proved in steps 2–3: additivity (B), and independence of the formula from the representation.

Notation. n = m + 1 and Hⁿ = μHE[n]. For an n-covector α and a linear map A, α ∘ ΛⁿA is the covector (v₁, …, vₙ) ↦ α(Av₁, …, Avₙ). For x ∈ O write Df(x) := fderiv ℝ f x. 𝒴 is the class of integer multiplicity Y ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with spt Y compact and contained in O. |α| is the Euclidean coefficient norm.

1. (Preliminaries.)
 (a) Let v₁, …, vₙ ∈ ℝ^P and let V be the P×n matrix with columns vᵢ. By multilinearity and the alternating property, α(v₁, …, vₙ) = Σ_I α(e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(n)})·det(V_I), the sum over strictly increasing I : {1, …, n} → {1, …, P}, where V_I is the n×n submatrix of rows I. By Cauchy–Schwarz, |α(v₁, …, vₙ)| ≤ |α|·(Σ_I det(V_I)²)^{1/2}. By the Cauchy–Binet formula Σ_I det(V_I)² = det(VᵀV), the Gram determinant, which is at most Π_i|vᵢ|² by Hadamard's inequality. Now let τ₁, …, τₙ be orthonormal, ζ = ±τ₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ τₙ, and vᵢ := Aτᵢ. Then |⟨α ∘ ΛⁿA, ζ⟩| = |α(Aτ₁, …, Aτₙ)| ≤ |α|·Π_i|Aτᵢ| ≤ |α|·‖A‖ⁿ. For n = 0 both sides equal |α|.
 (b) Let Y ∈ 𝒴, K := spt Y, and (M, θ, ξ) a representation of Y. Then Hⁿ(M ∖ K) = 0. Indeed ℝ^P ∖ K is open and Y vanishes on forms supported there (vanish_off_support), so μ_Y(ℝ^P ∖ K) = M_{ℝ^P∖K}(Y) = 0 (mass_eq_measure), and θ ≥ 1 on M.
 (c) Df is continuous on O ⊇ K, so Λ_K := sup_K ‖Df‖ < ∞. Also μ_Y(K) < ∞ by local finiteness of the weight.

2. (Definition and independence of the representation; Simon 2.24(2), 3.3.)
 (a) For Y ∈ 𝒴 with a representation (M, θ, ξ) and ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P), let I(ω) := ∫_M θ⟨ω(f(x)) ∘ ΛⁿDf(x), ξ(x)⟩ dHⁿ(x).
 (b) By 1(a)–(c) the integrand is bounded by θ·sup|ω|·Λ_Kⁿ·1_K Hⁿ-a.e. on M. So the integral exists, is linear in ω, and |I(ω)| ≤ sup|ω|·Λ_Kⁿ·μ_Y(K). Hence I is sequentially continuous on test forms (TestFormOnConverges gives uniform convergence) and defines a current.
 (c) I does not depend on the representation. Choose χ ∈ C_c^∞(O) with χ = 1 on a neighbourhood of K, and put β(x) := χ(x)·(ω(f(x)) ∘ ΛⁿDf(x)), a continuous compactly supported n-form. By 1(b), I(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨β, ξ⟩ dHⁿ. Mollifying β gives smooth β_k with supports in a fixed compact set and β_k → β uniformly. By dominated convergence ∫_M θ⟨β, ξ⟩ dHⁿ = lim_k ∫_M θ⟨β_k, ξ⟩ dHⁿ = lim_k Y(β_k), which depends only on Y.
 (d) Define push Y := I for Y ∈ 𝒴, and push Y := 0 for Y ∉ 𝒴. Then (i) holds for every representation.

3. ((B) additivity.) Let Y₁, Y₂ ∈ 𝒴 with supports K₁, K₂.
 (a) Y₁ − Y₂ is integer multiplicity (im_calculus (c)). It vanishes on every form whose support misses the compact set K₁ ∪ K₂ ⊆ O (vanish_off_support for Y₁ and Y₂). So spt(Y₁ − Y₂) is compact and contained in K₁ ∪ K₂ (support_of_vanishing), and Y₁ − Y₂ ∈ 𝒴.
 (b) Take χ = 1 near K₁ ∪ K₂ in step 2. Then push(Y₁ − Y₂)(ω) = lim_k (Y₁ − Y₂)(β_k) = lim_k Y₁(β_k) − lim_k Y₂(β_k) = push Y₁(ω) − push Y₂(ω).

4. ((iii) support; Simon 2.29.) Let Y ∈ 𝒴. f(K) is compact, since f is continuous on O ⊇ K. If tsupport ω ∩ f(K) = ∅, then ω(f(x)) = 0 for x ∈ K, so by 1(b) the integrand in (i) vanishes Hⁿ-a.e. on M and push Y(ω) = 0. By support_of_vanishing (with U = ℝ^P and the compact set f(K)), spt push Y ⊆ f(K) = f(spt Y).

5. ((iv) mass; Simon 2.29.) Let L satisfy ‖Df(y)‖ ≤ L for y ∈ O. If O ≠ ∅ then L ≥ 0; if O = ∅ then K = ∅, μ_Y = 0 and push Y = 0. For every admissible ω (|ω(y)| ≤ 1 for all y), by 1(a)(b): push Y(ω) ≤ ∫_M θ|ω(f(x))|·‖Df(x)‖ⁿ dHⁿ ≤ Lⁿ∫_M θ dHⁿ = Lⁿ·μ_Y(ℝ^P) = Lⁿ·M(Y), by mass_eq_measure with W = ℝ^P. Taking the supremum, M(push Y) ≤ Lⁿ·M(Y).

6. ((ii) integer multiplicity; Simon 3.5–3.9.) Let Y ∈ 𝒴 with representation (M, θ, ξ). By 1(b) we may replace M by M ∩ K.
 (a) Choose an open V with K ⊆ V and closure(V) ⊆ O compact. Near each point of closure(V), f is C¹ and Lipschitz.
 (b) On M the tangential differential d^M f_x : T_xM → ℝ^P exists Hⁿ-a.e., and d^M f_{x#}ξ(x) = Df(x)_#ξ(x), Df(x) restricted to T_xM (Simon Ch. 3, 2.2). So (i) reads push Y(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω(f(x)), d^M f_{x#}ξ(x)⟩ dHⁿ.
 (c) Let M₊ := {x ∈ M : J^M f(x) > 0}. Points with J^M f = 0 contribute nothing, since there d^M f_{x#}ξ(x) = 0 (3.4). Since |d^M f_{x#}ξ(x)| = J^M f(x), the area formula (Ch. 3, 2.5) gives (3.6):
 push Y(ω) = ∫_{f(M₊)} ⟨ω(y), Σ_{x ∈ f⁻¹(y)∩M₊} θ(x) d^M f_{x#}ξ(x)/|d^M f_{x#}ξ(x)|⟩ dHⁿ(y).
 (d) f(M₊) is countably n-rectifiable, as a union of Lipschitz images of the pieces of M on which f is Lipschitz. So for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ f(M₊) the approximate tangent space T_y f(M₊) exists. For Hⁿ-a.e. such y the set f⁻¹(y) ∩ M₊ is finite (2.4), and each vector d^M f_{x#}ξ(x)/|d^M f_{x#}ξ(x)| with x in it equals ±η(y), for a unit simple n-vector η(y) orienting T_y f(M₊) (3.7).
 (e) Hence (3.8) Σ_x θ(x) d^M f_{x#}ξ(x)/|…| = N(y)η(y) with N(y) ∈ ℤ. Replacing η by −η where N < 0, push Y = τ(f(M₊) ∩ {N ≠ 0}, |N|, η) (3.9).
 (f) The multiplicity is locally integrable: ∫_{f(M₊)} |N| dHⁿ ≤ ∫_{f(M₊)} Σ_x θ(x) dHⁿ(y) = ∫_M θ J^M f dHⁿ ≤ Λ_Kⁿ·μ_Y(K) < ∞ (area formula 2.5).
 (g) Choosing Borel versions of the carrier, N and η, this is an integer multiplicity triple in ℝ^P representing push Y. So push Y is integer multiplicity.

7. ((v) boundary; Simon 2.24(1), 2.29.) Let Y ∈ 𝒴 with ∂Y = 0, and V as in step 6.
 (a) Let χ₁ ∈ C_c^∞(O) with χ₁ = 1 on a neighbourhood of closure(V), and f_σ := (χ₁f) ∗ φ_σ for σ > 0 (mollification). Then f_σ is smooth on ℝ^P, and f_σ → f, Df_σ → Df uniformly on closure(V) as σ ↓ 0, because f is C¹ near closure(V).
 (b) For the smooth map g := f_σ, Simon 2.23 defines g_#Y(ω) := Y(ζ g^#ω) with ζ ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^P), ζ = 1 near K; the value does not depend on ζ.
 (c) By 2.24(1), ∂g_#Y = g_#∂Y = 0. Indeed ∂g_#Y(ω) = Y(ζ g^#dω) = Y(ζ d(g^#ω)) = Y(d(ζ g^#ω)) − Y(dζ ∧ g^#ω) = (∂Y)(ζ g^#ω) − 0 = 0, because dζ ∧ g^#ω vanishes near K = spt Y.
 (d) By 2.24(2), g_#Y(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω(f_σ(x)) ∘ ΛⁿDf_σ(x), ξ(x)⟩ dHⁿ. As σ ↓ 0 this tends to push Y(ω), by dominated convergence (uniform convergence on K and the bound of step 2).
 (e) Hence ∂(push Y)(ω) = push Y(dω) = lim_σ f_{σ#}Y(dω) = lim_σ ∂(f_{σ#}Y)(ω) = 0 for every ω. ∎
proof_key_steps: For Y with compact support K ⊆ O, push Y(ω) := ∫_M θ⟨ω(f(x)) ∘ ΛⁿDf(x), ξ(x)⟩ dHⁿ (2.24(2)) is a current. It does not depend on the representation (approximate the continuous form χ·f^#ω by smooth forms), and push Y := 0 otherwise.
Additivity follows from independence of the representation. The support lies in f(K), since the integrand vanishes off f⁻¹(spt ω).
Mass: |⟨α ∘ ΛⁿA, ξ⟩| ≤ |α|·‖A‖ⁿ (Cauchy–Binet, Hadamard) gives M(push Y) ≤ Lⁿ·M(Y).
Integer multiplicity by the area formula: push Y = τ(f(M₊), |N|, ±η) with N integer valued (3.6–3.9).
If ∂Y = 0 then ∂(push Y) = 0: push Y is the weak limit of push-forwards by smooth mollified maps, which commute with ∂ (2.24(1), 2.29).

subproblems.title: An integer multiplicity triple essentially carried by a compact set can be moved to a larger domain
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U, V ⊆ ℝ^P, and K ⊆ ℝ^P compact with K ⊆ V and K ⊆ U. Let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an IMRep of V (Simon 6.3.1 data in V) with Hⁿ(M ∖ K) = 0, where Hⁿ = μHE[n]. Then there is an IMRep R' of U with R'.carrier ⊆ K and R'.action ω = R.action ω for every n-form ω on ℝ^P. One can take R' = (M ∩ K, θ, ξ).

Accepted proof:
Source: step 6.6 of the parent proof (R̃ := (M_X ∩ K, θ_X, ξ_X) is an IMRep in U), with Simon 6.3.1 (chapter-06.txt lines 733–753). Uses the sibling dtc_approxTangent_of_null_diff, called (A) below. Let R' have carrier M ∩ K, multiplicity θ and orientation ξ.
1. M ∩ K and M are Hⁿ-a.e. equal: (M ∩ K) ∖ M = ∅, and M ∖ (M ∩ K) = M ∖ K is Hⁿ-null by hypothesis (ae_eq_set). Hence Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ K) = Hⁿ⌞M (Measure.restrict_congr_set).
2. Measurability: K is compact, hence closed and Borel, and M is Borel, so M ∩ K is Borel.
3. M ∩ K ⊆ K ⊆ U; this also gives R'.carrier ⊆ K.
4. Rectifiability: M ∩ K ⊆ M (CountablyRectifiable.mono).
5. θ is measurable, and θ(x) > 0 for x ∈ M ∩ K ⊆ M.
6. Local integrability in U. Let C be compact with C ⊆ U. Then (M ∩ K) ∩ C ⊆ M ∩ K, so ∫_{(M∩K)∩C} θ dHⁿ ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ (lintegral_mono_set). The right side is finite by the local integrability of R in V, applied to the compact set K ⊆ V.
7. ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ K), because Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ K) ≤ Hⁿ⌞M (AEStronglyMeasurable.mono_measure).
8. Orientation. For Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x, hence Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ K)-a.e. x (ae_restrict_of_ae_restrict_of_subset), there is Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q. Apply (A) with M' := M ∩ K ⊆ M and the open set ℝ^P (univ), which contains x: (M ∖ (M ∩ K)) ∩ ℝ^P = M ∖ K is Hⁿ-null. So HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (M ∩ K) x Q holds, with the same unit orientation ξ(x). Thus R' is an IMRep of U with carrier ⊆ K.
9. Action. For every n-form ω, R'.action ω = ∫ θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ d(Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ K)) = ∫ θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ d(Hⁿ⌞M) = R.action ω by step 1. The two measures are equal, so no integrability is needed. ∎
proof_key_steps: Take R' = (M ∩ K, θ, ξ). M ∩ K and M differ by the Hⁿ-null set M ∖ K, so Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ K) = Hⁿ⌞M and the actions coincide.
Local integrability in U follows from finiteness of the θ-integral over the compact set K ⊆ V.
The approximate tangent planes of M and M ∩ K agree because the sets differ by a null set (sibling A with the open set ℝ^P).
